(1) `declared_rhythm` floors to `absent`: generation.trigger is an UNPOPULATED field, and an unpopulated field is not a measured negative -- collapsing those two is the defect this wave exists to stop. (2) `actual_trigger` is MEASURED, and it is a stronger statement than 'no trigger was found' -- BUT IT IS SCOPED TO THE SURVIVING SET AND NOT BEYOND IT: the objects and metadata PRESENT AT THIS HOME were written by exactly ONE commit in one 3-second window. ⛔ THIS DOES NOT EXCLUDE AN EARLIER WRITE SINCE REPLACED OR EXPIRED -- snapshot expiry and overwrite both converge on one surviving snapshot, so 'only ever written once' would need the metadata log's snapshot HISTORY, not its current head, and that is UNMEASURED here. The cadence point does not rest on it: what carries the row is the surviving set plus the staleness. The discriminator is the Iceberg metadata tree, not the timestamps -- 1 snapshot object and 1 distinct write-commit uuid (48e4e347-6bc7-4499-aa3f-8a86a91f0ce4) across all 57 objects, so every data file belongs to one append. A one-shot write cannot be a cadence that failed, and it does not become one by ageing. Timestamps corroborate: first 2026-07-08T15:51:14.000Z, last 2026-07-08T15:51:17.000Z, 1 distinct write-day. ⛔ WHY the run happened, and whether anyone intended it to repeat, is UNMEASURED.

key.evidence: ⛔ THE FINDING IN THIS CARD, AND IT IS `inferred` ON PURPOSE. MEASURED: two S3 homes exist under warehouse/globgrph/ whose table-name component is identically `cse_test`, differing only in uuid -- this one (24458e6c, written 2026-07-08) and bb57a916 (written 2026-07-08). Their key sets are disjoint. INFERRED: pyiceberg/Nessie assigns a NEW uuid-suffixed location on each create_table, and a namespace admits one table per name, so two locations for one name is consistent with a create -> drop -> create cycle in which at most ONE of these homes is still reachable by the catalog key and the other is an ORPHANED physical location. ⛔ UNMEASURED, AND IT IS THE DECIDING FACT: which home the catalog resolves to today, or whether either is still registered. The Nessie catalog is not reachable from this seat, so this card CANNOT say which of the two is live and does not guess. Settling it needs one catalog.load_table((globgrph, 'cse_test')) read of its metadata location. ⛔ THIS CARD DOES NOT CLASSIFY THE ORPHAN AS A DEFECT -- naming it is the carder's job, deciding it is the owner's.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: A true absence returns KeyCount=0 at rc=0 -- a failed retrieval returns a VALUE, not an error. And at THIS subject a wrong home does not even return 0: the same-named sibling returns a populated census
failure_mode.evidence: FOUR read-only probe classes, each a SEPARATE invocation, rc read UNPIPED. MEASURED: (1) true absence -- real bucket, bogus prefix -> rc=0 out='0'; (2) wrong bucket -> rc=255 out='An error occurred (NoSuchBucket) when calling the ListObject', an ERROR, not a zero; (3) wrong region -> rc=0 out='1'; (4) near-miss prefix, this home's own uuid tail mutated -> rc=0 out='0'. So among the exercised classes a zero is produced by absence and by a wrong prefix, and NOT by a wrong bucket. ⛔ THE FIFTH CLASS -- a missing s3:ListBucket -- WAS NOT EXERCISED and may also return a zero; that unexercised class is the SOLE ground on which distinguishable_from_true_negative is `no` at basis `inferred`. An unscoped 'only a true absence produces a zero' would contradict this same row. ⛔ AND AT THIS SUBJECT THE SHARPEST FAILURE IS NOT A ZERO AT ALL: because the sibling home is real and populated, a home confused between the two returns a healthy KeyCount=1 and a full census, so every arm passes while the card describes the wrong table. That class is caught structurally by refuse_sibling_confusion() at build time, not by reading a count.

verdict.why: NOT LOAD-BEARING, on the evidence gathered here: an isolated test-harness table whose SURVIVING objects were written in a single 3-second append on 2026-07-08 with no later surviving write, 53 days stale at carding. It is carded because it EXISTS in the manifest and consumes a real S3 home, not because anything was shown to read it. QUALIFIED, and these are the qualifications: the materializer is `inferred` -- the invocation that created this table was never found, and the partition-spec match identifies a writer CLASS, not a run; the `key` row carries an UNRESOLVED identity question, since two homes share the table name `cse_test` and this seat cannot reach the Nessie catalog to say which one it addresses -- so one of the two may be an orphaned location and this card does not claim which; coverage spans the OBJECT plane only and NO row was read, so whether this table's rows duplicate the production cse store's is UNMEASURED; and whether any consumer reads it, or is harmed by it existing, is UNMEASURED here. ⛔ THIS CARD DOES NOT CLASSIFY THE TABLE AS DEBT AND DOES NOT PROPOSE DROPPING IT: --drop permits it and the production guard would refuse the real log, but that is a permission, not a recommendation. Naming the state is the carder's job; deciding it is the owner's.
